correctness.rationale: Proof is self-contained: token adjacency yields an exact necessary-and-sufficient three-part dominating-set criterion; with k isolated B-vertices it gives x+z>=n-k+binom(k,2)>=n-1, so equality has y<=1. For y=1 equality forces precisely the 3*binom(n,2) ordinary constructions. For y=0 the condition on every uncovered B-vertex forces t=0 and k=2, n=4, z=x=2, yielding exactly the 36 injection constructions. Both families satisfy the criterion; no smaller set exists. All 47,432,132 possible size-n labelled subsets at n=3..7 were exhaustively tested by a separately written C++17 token-graph checker, with counts 9,54,30,45,63. The finite checks are not substituted for the quantified infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact number and symmetry type of all optimal dominating configurations is a natural refinement of the recently established minimum size. The 4-column graph has 36 additional optimal sets, doubling the standard count 18 to 54 and creating a second distinct orbit, whereas every other n>=3 has a rigid single family. These features quantify optimization degeneracy and permit exact random sampling, but are not inferred from knowing gamma=n. It is a complete infinite classification, not an arbitrary small fixed-parameter experiment.
